I work on converting natural-language text into first-order logic (NL→FOL, autoformalization) with
LLM pipelines. Evaluation is the bottleneck. Correct FOL for a sentence is not unique — different
predicate names, different decompositions of the same concept, and logically equivalent rewrites can
all be correct. Gold FOL annotations are rare and expensive. The metrics in use either need a gold
formula (exact match, BLEU, prover-checked equivalence to the gold) or only check that the output
parses. In my own pilot I used cheap structural metrics: whether a set of generated formulas loads
together without conflicts, whether predicate arities stay consistent, how many predicates are used
but never defined, and how similar the predicate sets are across reruns. Those measure stability and
composability, not whether a formula says what the sentence says.

Find new metrics for NL→FOL output quality. Operating situation: you are given a natural-language
sentence (or short passage) and a candidate FOL formalization produced by any system. There is no gold
formula, no ontology or controlled vocabulary, and no domain knowledge. The metric returns a score
that predicts whether the formalization is faithful to the text, and ideally which kind of error it
contains (quantifier or scope error, dropped or added condition, negation/polarity error, swapped
arguments, conflated or wrongly split concepts). Metrics may score a single formula or a set (several
samples for one sentence, or the formalizations of all sentences in one document). They must be
task-agnostic — usable for any NL→FOL setting, not tied to a domain, dataset or pipeline — and cheap
enough to run on every output (solver calls and small models are fine; a large-LLM judge per formula
only if shown to earn its cost).

Requirements:
- Keep the target fixed: the metric must predict faithfulness to the text. Detecting synthetic
  perturbations, parse validity, or run-to-run stability are not substitutes for that target.
- Validate against ground truth, never against the metric itself. Use public datasets with gold
  sentence-level FOL (e.g. FOLIO, MALLS, or others you find) to build a meta-evaluation set: real
  candidate formalizations from several different systems, plus controlled perturbations of gold
  formulas with known error types, labelled via prover-checked equivalence to gold. Handle two known
  problems: some gold annotations are wrong, and a candidate can be correct without being equivalent
  to the gold (different vocabulary or granularity). Estimate how often each happens and how it
  biases the labels. These datasets are public, so check whether LLM-based metrics benefit from having
  seen the gold.
- For each metric report: correlation with correctness at item and system level; sensitivity per error
  type; invariance under meaning-preserving rewrites (variable/predicate renaming, reordering,
  equivalent restatements); coverage — unparseable outputs are counted and reported, never silently
  dropped; and cost.
- Compare against baselines: parse/compile rate, round-trip (FOL→NL→compare) similarity,
  LLM-as-judge, sampling self-consistency, and the structural consistency metrics described above. A
  new metric matters only if it adds signal those don't.
- Report how each metric's reliability changes with sentence complexity (length, number of quantifiers,
  nesting depth, number of conditions and exceptions). Long, heavily conditioned sentences matter most
  to me.
- Negative results are welcome: if a family of metrics does not track correctness, show that clearly.

Out of scope: comparing grounded vs ungrounded generation (ontology vocabulary injected into prompts),
anything that depends on a particular ontology, and building a better NL→FOL translator. The
contribution is the measurement, not the translator.

Deliverables: reusable Python functions taking (text, fol) — or a set of such pairs — each with a
precise statement of what it measures; the meta-evaluation dataset with its labels; and the results.

I appended a pilot study of this problem with some metrics I already used but haven't verified. Just for reference.

\\\\\n\\midrule\nflash-lite judge (disg.) & 0.642 [0.607, 0.676] & 5.1e-5 \\\\\nflash-lite judge (orig.) & 0.623 [0.593, 0.651] & 5.1e-5 \\\\\nnano judge (disg.) & 0.644 [0.609, 0.680] & 2.0e-5 \\\\\nlocal judge Qwen-8B (disg.) & 0.674 [0.646, 0.703] & -- \\\\\n\\midrule\nround-trip NLI (min) & 0.606 [0.569, 0.645] & 2.8e-5 \\\\\nself-consistency (5-sample) & 0.598 [0.559, 0.637] & 6.7e-5 \\\\\n\\midrule\n28-feature stack & 0.735 [0.699, 0.766] & -- \\\\\n28-feature stack + c\\_score\\_align & 0.774 [0.743, 0.802] & -- \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe drop from 0.952 (shared signature, R\\_COMP-SIG) to 0.741 (free vocabulary, $E$) reflects the cost of predicate-name alignment: the aligner introduces both false negatives (correct equivalences missed) and false positives (incorrect mappings endorsed).\nAligner-free consensus (c\\_exact) achieves 0.689 [0.652, 0.726], indicating that roughly half of the free-vocabulary signal comes from the aligner and half from structural agreement alone.\n\nOn L25 sentences alone ($\\geq$25 words), the advantage narrows to $\\Delta = +0.069$ [$-$0.020, +0.148], not significant at the 95\\% level.\nThis foreshadows the length-dependent degradation described in Section~\\ref{sec:mechanism}.\n\n\\paragraph{Frontier judge comparison.}\nOn the 284-row subsample scored by the frontier judge (Gemini~3.1~Pro), c\\_score\\_align achieves 95.7\\% of the frontier judge's AUROC (ratio 0.957 [0.887, 1.034]).\n\n\\paragraph{System-level ranking.}\nThe consensus metric achieves Kendall $\\tau_b = 0.692$ [+0.513, +0.795] between system mean score and R\\_AB error rate across 13 system$\\times$variant configurations, comparable to the best judges.\n\n\\subsection{Free-vocabulary out-of-sample (R\\_COMP FREE)}\\label{sec:free_oos}\n\nThe same 221~R\\_COMP sentences were also translated under free vocabulary (each translator choosing its own predicate names).\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_-tTYmHVAOMOt/round-5/experiment-13}}\nConfirmatory labelling required a gloss gate (LLM-checked semantic alignment of predicate mappings).\nThis gate failed twice (balanced accuracy 0.776 and 0.561, below the 0.90 threshold), producing zero confirmed CORRECT rows and rendering the confirmatory test not testable.\n\nUnder provisional non-confirmatory labels (ERROR\\_CERT vs.\\ MAPPED, where MAPPED is an upper bound on CORRECT), Table~\\ref{tab:free} reports the untouched results.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{R\\_COMP FREE provisional AUROCs (within-template, untouched rows). Labels are non-confirmatory.}\n\\label{tab:free}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\nView & $n$ (ERR/MAPPED) & c\\_align & judge \\\\\n\\midrule\nDisguised & 1706 (602/1104) & 0.801 [0.770, 0.834] & 0.584 [0.550, 0.618] \\\\\nOriginal & 1709 (605/1104) & 0.804 [0.774, 0.836] & 0.633 [0.601, 0.666] \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe disguised-judge delta is $+0.217$ [+0.175, +0.260]; the original-view delta is $+0.171$ [+0.135, +0.206].\nOn a 146-row subset with independent two-auditor labels, consensus achieves $\\Delta = +0.105$ [+0.011, +0.215] over the original-view judge.\nOn a 150-row frontier-judge subsample, consensus reaches 0.94 of the frontier judge's AUROC (ratio 0.940 [0.825, 1.056]).\n\nThese provisional numbers cannot count as confirmation because the MAPPED labels conflate vocabulary-alignment failures with genuine correctness.\nThey are consistent with the development-set signal but independent confirmation requires a working gloss gate or a different labelling strategy.\n\n\\subsection{Mechanism}\\label{sec:mechanism}\n\nWe decompose the consensus signal\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_-tTYmHVAOMOt/round-3/evaluation-2}} into two components at a fixed decision threshold:\n\\begin{itemize}\n\\item \\textbf{Endorsement} $e$: fraction of ERROR items endorsed by the peer majority (false negatives of consensus).\n\\item \\textbf{Divergence} $d$: fraction of CORRECT items that diverge from the peer majority (false positives of consensus).\n\\end{itemize}\nThe consensus AUROC at a binary threshold equals $1 - (e + d)/2$, so both quantities must be small for the metric to work.\n\n\\paragraph{Shared vocabulary: both components near zero.}\nOn R\\_COMP-SIG, $e = 0.0$ and $d = 0.260$: no error escapes detection.\nThe false-alarm rate of 0.260 arises from correct translations that use valid but structurally different formalizations.\n\n\\paragraph{Free vocabulary: divergence degrades with length.}\nAs Figure~\\ref{fig:complexity} shows, on development set~$E$ the net consensus degradation from short to long sentences is $\\Delta(e+d) = +0.356$ [+0.198, +0.493], driven almost entirely by divergence ($\\Delta d = +0.608$, $\\Delta e = -0.252$): correct translations of long sentences increasingly disagree with their peers, not because of vocabulary mismatches, but because independent models make different structural choices for complex quantifier scopes and exception clauses.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_complexity_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Decomposition of free-vocabulary consensus error rates by sentence-length tercile on development set~$E$. Endorsement rate $e$ (errors incorrectly endorsed by peers) decreases with length, but divergence rate $d$ (correct items incorrectly flagged) increases sharply, producing net degradation of +0.356 from the shortest to the longest tercile. Under shared signature (R\\_COMP-SIG), this degradation is absent.}\n  \\label{fig:complexity}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\paragraph{Family sufficiency.}\nThree peer families suffice for 97\\% of full-pool AUROC ($k_{95} = 3$), but the long-sentence tercile requires $k_{95} = 5$ (Table~\\ref{tab:k_families} and Figure~\\ref{fig:k_curve}).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Free-vocabulary AUROC by number of peer families on development set $E$.}\n\\label{tab:k_families}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{ccc}\n\\toprule\n$k$ & AUROC (overall) & AUROC (long, T3) \\\\\n\\midrule\n1 & 0.685 & 0.581 \\\\\n3 & 0.757 & 0.651 \\\\\n5 & 0.776 & 0.698 \\\\\n7 & 0.784 & 0.726 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_k_curve_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Stratified AUROC as a function of the number of peer families $k$, for the full development set (solid blue) and the long-sentence tercile (dashed red). Three families capture 97\\% of the full-pool signal, but long sentences require five families to reach 95\\%.}\n  \\label{fig:k_curve}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\subsection{Confirmation status}\\label{sec:confirmation}\n\nIndependent confirmation on held-out data remains incomplete.\nA fresh held-out dataset (E2-A, 550~new sentences) was constructed, but the run-level budget was exhausted before enough items could be labelled.\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_-tTYmHVAOMOt/round-4/dataset-4}}\nOn the one testable stratum (DT, short sentences from ProverQA), consensus achieves a stratified AUROC of 0.916, tying the local Qwen-8B judge ($\\Delta = +0.003$ [$-$0.042, +0.052]).\nOn L25 sentences, c\\_score\\_align falls to 0.443 on only 42 items (35~ERROR~/~7~CORRECT), below chance, but the estimate has extreme variance with only 7~CORRECT items from 3~sentences.\nEvery pre-registered criterion on the target strata returned NOT\\_TESTABLE or unfavourable.\n\n\\subsection{The rename tradeoff}\\label{sec:rename}\n\nThe predicate aligner\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_-tTYmHVAOMOt/round-3/experiment-8}} that enables cross-family comparison under free vocabulary also introduces a fundamental false-alarm vulnerability.\nWhen correct formulas are copied with meaning-preserving predicate renames (same semantics, different symbol names), the consensus score should not change.\nTable~\\ref{tab:rename} shows the false-alarm rates in practice.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{False-alarm (FA) rates on meaning-preserving renames of CORRECT candidates. NONCE = random nonsense names; SYN = WordNet synonyms. Flip = FA induced by the rename alone (FA minus base FA).}\n\\label{tab:rename}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nMetric & NONCE FA & NONCE flip & SYN FA & SYN flip \\\\\n\\midrule\nc\\_align & 0.765 & 0.605 & 0.565 & 0.313 \\\\\nc\\_nf (name-free) & 0.132 & 0.000 & 0.201 & 0.000 \\\\\np\\_peer\\_text & 1.000 & 0.821 & 0.216 & 0.080 \\\\\njudge (disg.) & 0.229 & 0.134 & 0.085 & 0.058 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe name-free variant c\\_nf eliminates rename sensitivity (flip = 0) but at the cost of blindness to meaning-rename errors (within-base AUROC 0.499, chance level) and lower overall discrimination (strat AUROC 0.686 vs.\\ 0.741).\nThis tradeoff explains the gap between shared-signature and free-vocabulary performance: the shared signature eliminates the need for alignment entirely, sidestepping the rename problem.\n\n\\subsection{Per-type sensitivity}\n\nOn the PERTURB suite (4,234 typed mutants + 868 controls from development data), consensus recall at the primary threshold is flat across error operators: NEG 0.761, SWAP 0.758, DROP 0.721, ADD 0.763, MEANING\\_RENAME 0.762.\nPer-operator AUROC within error types cannot be computed because 94--100\\% of mutants receive the maximum consensus score, a ceiling effect of the endorsement structure.\n\nError typing outside a shared vocabulary is negative: the free-vocabulary typing accuracy is 0.123 [0.081, 0.169] on $E$, comparable to the judge (0.326) and the peer-medoid baseline (0.328) only when all metrics are near chance.\n\n\\subsection{Dead ends}\n\nSeveral alternatives were investigated and abandoned during development: a fused structural-feature filter (false-alarm gate failure); name-free consensus c\\_nf (rename-invariant but blind to meaning-rename errors, as described in Section~\\ref{sec:rename}); a decomposed solver-based semantic reader (balanced accuracy 0.476); LLM adjudication of disputed items (balanced accuracy 0.662 on expert-labelled items); and candidate-signature consensus, which scores candidates by cueing peers with the candidate's own predicate symbols rather than letting them choose independently (provisional negative: error endorsement rose to 0.459 because peers were anchored into reproducing the candidate's errors).\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_-tTYmHVAOMOt/round-4/experiment-9}}\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\n\\subsection{Shared versus free vocabulary}\n\nThe central finding is that vocabulary regime governs metric strength.\nUnder shared signature, consensus achieves near-perfect discrimination (0.954 AUROC) flat across sentence lengths.\nUnder free vocabulary, performance drops by roughly 0.15~AUROC on comparable sentences (R\\_COMP-SIG 0.952 versus R\\_COMP FREE 0.801, both within-template on long composed sentences) and degrades with sentence length on natural data.\n\nThis gap is explained by the rename tradeoff: the predicate-name aligner needed for free-vocabulary comparison introduces both false negatives (missed equivalences) and false positives (spurious mappings), and these grow worse as formulas become longer and more structurally diverse.\nThe practical implication is that consensus-based evaluation is most reliable when translators share a predicate vocabulary, as in controlled evaluation settings~\\citep{Bayless2025,Vossel2025}.\n\n\\subsection{Why confirmation is incomplete}\n\nThe confirmation attempt was defeated by two independent problems: (1)~insufficient fresh data (the E2-A budget was stopped before enough correct items accumulated in the long-sentence strata), and (2)~a broken labelling gate (the gloss-based semantic alignment required for R\\_COMP FREE labels failed quality checks twice).\nNeither failure refutes the development-set signal, but neither allows us to confirm it on the target strata.\n\nThe E2-A L25 result (AUROC 0.443, near chance, on 42~items) is concerning but difficult to interpret: with only 7~CORRECT items from 3~sentences, the estimate has extreme variance and a single sentence can dominate.\nWe report it for completeness but note that it does not meet any standard testability criterion.\n\n\\subsection{The rename tradeoff as a fundamental limit}\n\nThe rename tradeoff is not a bug in our aligner but a structural property of cross-family consensus under independent vocabulary.\nAny alignment procedure that maps independently chosen predicate names to a common vocabulary will sometimes map semantically distinct predicates together, endorsing meaning-rename errors.\nEliminating the alignment (c\\_exact, c\\_nf) preserves rename invariance but sacrifices the structural comparison that drives error detection.\n\nWe conjecture that resolving this tradeoff requires either (a)~a shared predicate vocabulary supplied to all translators, which eliminates the problem entirely but restricts the evaluation to controlled settings~\\citep{Bayless2025,Vossel2025}, or (b)~a semantic disambiguation step (such as natural-language glosses of each predicate) that could break the alignment ambiguity.\nOur attempt at option~(b), a gloss gate using LLM-generated explanations of predicate meanings, failed quality checks, leaving this direction open.\n\n\\subsection{Limitations}\\label{sec:limitations}\n\n\\begin{enumerate}\n\\item \\textbf{Shared-signature scope.} The 0.954 AUROC result uses templated sentences with a supplied predicate vocabulary, which eliminates the alignment problem. The templates and the supplied signature limit the scope of this result to controlled evaluation settings.\n\\item \\textbf{Development data overlap.} The R\\_COMP-SIG dataset later served as development data for aligner tuning. The pre-registration ensures the SIG result itself is uncontaminated, but the development-set numbers from $E$ are not independent.\n\\item \\textbf{Rename vulnerability.} Under free vocabulary, a 76.5\\% false-alarm rate on nonce renames means the metric will systematically penalise any translation that uses non-standard predicate names, even if semantically correct.\n\\item \\textbf{Length degradation (free vocabulary).} Consensus discrimination degrades with sentence length under free vocabulary (NET $+0.356$), driven by correct-translation divergence. The metric is weakest on the longest, most complex sentences, precisely the cases where gold-free evaluation is most needed.\n\\item \\textbf{Provisional labels.} R\\_COMP FREE results use provisional (non-confirmatory) labels; the two-auditor subset ($\\Delta = +0.105$) has a CI that barely excludes zero.\n\\item \\textbf{Label dependence.} Development results on~$E$ depend on a three-person panel whose agreement is imperfect (disputed items exist in every stratum). The metric's advantage could partly reflect alignment with panel biases rather than with ground-truth faithfulness.\n\\item \\textbf{Cost.} The consensus metric requires generating $k$ peer translations per sentence, costing \\$0.91 per 10{,}000 candidates (amortised) at $k = 9$; a single cheap judge call costs \\$0.51 per 10{,}000.\n\\item \\textbf{Domain.} All results are on English$\\to$FOL from MALLS, ProverQA, and R\\_COMP sources. Generalisation to other logic formalisms, languages, or sentence distributions is untested.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\nCross-family solver consensus is a strong gold-free faithfulness metric for NL$\\to$FOL translation when translators share a predicate vocabulary.\nThe pre-registered R\\_COMP-SIG result (AUROC 0.954 versus 0.587 for a disguised judge, flat with length) establishes the ceiling; free vocabulary costs roughly 0.15~AUROC and introduces the rename tradeoff.\n\nUnder free vocabulary, consensus still outperforms cheap LLM judges on both development data ($+0.099$) and untouched out-of-sample sentences ($+0.171$), and adds information beyond structural and statistical baselines.\nThe mechanism --- errors scatter while correct translations cluster --- provides an intuitive explanation grounded in the diversity of independent formalizations.\n\nHowever, independent confirmation on held-out data was budget-stopped and remains incomplete, the rename tradeoff limits applicability to free-vocabulary settings, and discrimination degrades with sentence length under free vocabulary.\nWe release the full evaluation code and data to enable reproduction.\nThe immediate open problems are: (1)~completing the fresh-data confirmation with adequate sample sizes; (2)~breaking the rename tradeoff, perhaps through semantic predicate glossing; and (3)~understanding why correct translations of complex sentences diverge under free vocabulary even when no vocabulary mismatch exists.\n\n\\bibliographystyle{plainnat}\n\\bibliography{references}\n\n\\end{document}\n", "numLines": 436, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 436}}

<main id="main">

<header class="hero">
  <h1>Cross-Family Solver Consensus as a Gold-Free Faithfulness Metric for NL-to-FOL Translation</h1>
  <div class="hero-meta">Anonymous &middot; Preliminary Study</div>
  <div class="hero-tldr">
    <strong>TL;DR</strong> &mdash; If independent LLM families translate the same sentence into first-order logic and an SMT solver checks pairwise equivalence, the fraction of peers that disagree with a candidate predicts whether it is faithful to the text. Under shared predicate vocabulary this reaches 0.954 AUROC; under free vocabulary it achieves 0.741 stratified AUROC, outperforming LLM judges by +0.099 on development data without any gold references.
  </div>
  <div class="hero-links">
    <a href="paper.pdf" target="_blank">Paper PDF</a>
    <a href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic" target="_blank">Code repository</a>
  </div>
</header>

<section id="contributions">
  <h2>Contributions</h2>
  <div class="contrib-grid">
    <div class="contrib-card">
      <h3>Shared-signature ceiling</h3>
      <p>Pre-registered evaluation on 221 long-exception sentences: consensus AUROC 0.954 versus 0.587 for a disguised judge (&Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.367), flat across word-length terciles, with zero error endorsement.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="contrib-card">
      <h3>Free-vocabulary signal</h3>
      <p>On development set&nbsp;E (2,686 items), consensus outperforms judges by &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.099 on stratified AUROC. Aligner-free consensus (c_exact) reaches 0.689 without any predicate mapping.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="contrib-card">
      <h3>Out-of-sample transfer</h3>
      <p>On untouched R_COMP&nbsp;FREE sentences under provisional labels: &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.171 versus the original-view judge; consensus reaches 0.94 of the frontier judge's AUROC.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="contrib-card">
      <h3>Rename tradeoff</h3>
      <p>A 76.5% false-alarm rate under nonce predicate renames that no variant could eliminate without sacrificing error recall, identifying a fundamental limit of free-vocabulary consensus.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="method">
  <h2>Method</h2>

  <h3>Consensus scoring</h3>
  <p>Given a sentence and a candidate FOL translation, collect peer translations from <em>k</em> independent LLM families. Each peer uses the same few-shot prompt but a different base model (Gemini, Claude, GPT, Llama, Qwen, Phi, Mistral). The consensus score is:</p>
  <p style="text-align:center; font-family: var(--serif); font-size: 1.05rem; margin-block: 0.75rem;">
    c_score(c, s) = 1 &minus; (1/k) &Sigma; <b>1</b>[equiv(c, p<sub>i</sub>)]
  </p>
  <p>Under <strong>shared signature</strong>, all translators use a supplied predicate vocabulary and equiv is a direct Z3 check. Under <strong>free vocabulary</strong>, each translator chooses its own predicate names and equiv requires a predicate-name aligner before the Z3 check.</p>

  <h3>Predicate alignment</h3>
  <p>Independent translators choose different names for the same concept (e.g., <code>Runs(x)</code> vs. <code>IsRunner(x)</code>). The aligner combines three cost components: <strong>structural cost</strong> (polarity profile, argument-count match, nesting depth), <strong>text-anchor cost</strong> (overlap between predicate-name words and source-sentence tokens via Porter stemming and WordNet), and <strong>semantic signature</strong> (truth-value profiles over random finite interpretations). The <em>k</em> cheapest bijections are evaluated, and the pair is declared equivalent if any bijection yields Z3-verified equivalence.</p>

  <h3>Score variants</h3>
  <p><code>c_exact</code>: no alignment, exact-match equivalence only. Immune to rename false alarms but blind to vocabulary-differing equivalences. <code>c_nf</code> (name-free): alignment by structural and semantic signatures only, ignoring text anchoring. <code>p_peer_text</code>: logistic fusion of consensus features with text-side features (bag-of-words coverage, role accounting, Z3 structural match).</p>

  <h3>Evaluation framework</h3>
  <p><strong>Shared-signature labels</strong> come from Z3 equivalence to trusted-by-construction references, with no human or LLM judgement in the labelling loop. <strong>Free-vocabulary labels</strong> on development set&nbsp;E come from a three-person expert panel (adjudicated as ERROR or CORRECT). The primary metric is <strong>stratified AUROC</strong>: items are paired only within the same source stratum, eliminating confounds from stratum-level base rates. Confidence intervals use sentence-cluster percentile bootstrap (B&nbsp;=&nbsp;2,000).</p>
</section>

<section id="results">
  <h2>Results</h2>

  <div class="big-nums">

    </div>
    <div class="big-num">
      <div class="val">0.741</div>
      <div class="label">Consensus AUROC<br>(free vocabulary, dev)</div>
    </div>
    <div class="big-num">

    </div>
  </div>

  <section id="sig-results">
    <h3>Shared-signature results (R_COMP-SIG)</h3>
    <p class="table-cap">Table 1: Within-template AUROC on R_COMP-SIG (221 sentences, pure Z3 labels). CIs are 95% sentence-cluster bootstrap.</p>
    <div class="table-wrap">
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>n</th><th>AUROC [95% CI]</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>c_score_sig</code></td><td>2024</td><td>0.952 [0.937, 0.965]</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>c_score_align</code></td><td>2024</td><td>0.952 [0.937, 0.965]</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Judge (frontier, orig.)</td><td>60</td><td>0.932 [0.782, 1.000]</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Judge (flash-lite, orig.)</td><td>1932</td><td>0.673 [0.637, 0.708]</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Judge (flash-lite, disg.)</td><td>1904</td><td>0.587 [0.551, 0.622]</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Judge (local, disg.)</td><td>2024</td><td>0.498 [0.459, 0.534]</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
    <p>On 1,904 rows where both scores exist, consensus achieves &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.367 [+0.328, +0.404] over the disguised flash-lite judge. Error endorsement is zero: every error item receives a consensus score of 1.0 (maximum divergence).</p>

    <p><strong>Flat with sentence length.</strong> Unlike the free-vocabulary setting, consensus under shared signature is flat across word-length terciles:</p>
    <div class="table-wrap">
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Tercile</th><th>n</th><th>ERR/COR</th><th>c_sig</th><th>Judge (disg.)</th><th>&Delta; [CI]</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>W1 (shortest)</td><td>574</td><td>125/449</td><td>0.959</td><td>0.578</td><td>+0.382 [+0.278, +0.472]</td></tr>
          <tr><td>W2</td><td>743</td><td>149/594</td><td>0.947</td><td>0.624</td><td>+0.331 [+0.253, +0.421]</td></tr>
          <tr><td>W3 (longest)</td><td>707</td><td>155/552</td><td>0.953</td><td>0.567</td><td>+0.388 [+0.301, +0.471]</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
    <p>On a descriptive 60-row stratified subsample scored by the frontier judge (Gemini 3.1 Pro, original view), consensus achieves pooled AUROC 0.956 [0.889, 1.000] versus 0.932 [0.855, 0.990] for the frontier judge.</p>
  </section>

  <section id="dev-results">
    <h3>Free-vocabulary development results (set E)</h3>
    <p class="table-cap">Table 2: Stratified AUROC on development set E (R_AB population, free vocabulary, n&nbsp;=&nbsp;2,686). Higher is better.</p>
    <div class="table-wrap">
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>Strat AUROC [95% CI]</th><th>$/item</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>c_score_align</code></td><td>0.741 [0.705, 0.775]</td><td>9.1e-5</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>p_peer_text</code> (fused)</td><td>0.753 [0.720, 0.784]</td><td>9.1e-5</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>c_exact</code> (no alignment)</td><td>0.689 [0.652, 0.726]</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>c_nf</code> (name-free)</td><td>0.686 [0.647, 0.720]</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>
          <tr><td colspan="3" style="border:none; padding:0.25rem"></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Flash-lite judge (disg.)</td><td>0.642 [0.607, 0.676]</td><td>5.1e-5</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Flash-lite judge (orig.)</td><td>0.623 [0.593, 0.651]</td><td>5.1e-5</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Nano judge (disg.)</td><td>0.644 [0.609, 0.680]</td><td>2.0e-5</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Local judge Qwen-8B (disg.)</td><td>0.674 [0.646, 0.703]</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>
          <tr><td colspan="3" style="border:none; padding:0.25rem"></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Round-trip NLI (min)</td><td>0.606 [0.569, 0.645]</td><td>2.8e-5</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Self-consistency (5-sample)</td><td>0.598 [0.559, 0.637]</td><td>6.7e-5</td></tr>
          <tr><td colspan="3" style="border:none; padding:0.25rem"></td></tr>
          <tr><td>28-feature stack</td><td>0.735 [0.699, 0.766]</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>
          <tr><td>28-feature stack + <code>c_score_align</code></td><td>0.774 [0.743, 0.802]</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
    <p>Cross-family consensus outperforms the disguised flash-lite judge by &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.099 [+0.049, +0.146] on the full R_AB population and by &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.116 [+0.070, +0.163] on the long-sentence pool (L25+L20+EXC). Adding <code>c_score_align</code> to the 28-feature baseline stack increases stratified AUROC by +0.039 [+0.021, +0.057]; a permutation null test gives p<sub>95</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.009.</p>
    <p>The drop from 0.952 (shared signature) to 0.741 (free vocabulary) reflects the cost of predicate-name alignment. Aligner-free consensus (<code>c_exact</code>) at 0.689 indicates that roughly half of the free-vocabulary signal comes from structural agreement alone.</p>
    <p>On L25 sentences alone, the advantage narrows to &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.069 [&minus;0.020, +0.148], not significant at the 95% level. The frontier judge comparison on a 284-row subsample shows <code>c_score_align</code> at 95.7% of the frontier judge's AUROC (ratio 0.957 [0.887, 1.034]).</p>
    <p>System-level ranking: Kendall &tau;<sub>b</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.692 [+0.513, +0.795] between system mean score and R_AB error rate across 13 system&times;variant configurations.</p>
  </section>

  <section id="oos-results">
    <h3>Free-vocabulary out-of-sample (R_COMP FREE)</h3>
    <p class="table-cap">Table 3: R_COMP FREE provisional AUROCs (within-template, untouched rows). Labels are non-confirmatory.</p>
    <div class="table-wrap">
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>View</th><th>n (ERR/MAPPED)</th><th>c_align</th><th>Judge</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Disguised</td><td>1706 (602/1104)</td><td>0.801 [0.770, 0.834]</td><td>0.584 [0.550, 0.618]</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Original</td><td>1709 (605/1104)</td><td>0.804 [0.774, 0.836]</td><td>0.633 [0.601, 0.666]</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
    <p>The disguised-judge delta is +0.217 [+0.175, +0.260]; the original-view delta is +0.171 [+0.135, +0.206]. On a 146-row subset with independent two-auditor labels, &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.105 [+0.011, +0.215]. On a 150-row frontier-judge subsample, consensus reaches 0.94 of the frontier judge's AUROC (ratio 0.940 [0.825, 1.056]).</p>
    <p>These provisional numbers cannot count as confirmation because the MAPPED labels conflate vocabulary-alignment failures with genuine correctness.</p>
  </section>

  <section id="mechanism">
    <h3>Mechanism</h3>
    <p>The consensus signal decomposes into endorsement <em>e</em> (fraction of ERROR items endorsed by the peer majority) and divergence <em>d</em> (fraction of CORRECT items flagged). On R_COMP-SIG, <em>e</em>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.0 and <em>d</em>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.260: no error escapes detection.</p>
    <p>Under free vocabulary on development set E, the net degradation from short to long sentences is &Delta;(e+d)&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.356 [+0.198, +0.493], driven almost entirely by divergence (&Delta;d&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.608, &Delta;e&nbsp;=&nbsp;&minus;0.252). Correct translations of long sentences increasingly disagree with their peers due to different structural choices for complex quantifier scopes and exception clauses.</p>

    <p><strong>Family sufficiency.</strong> Three peer families suffice for 97% of full-pool AUROC (k<sub>95</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;3), but the long-sentence tercile requires k<sub>95</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;5.</p>
    <p class="table-cap">Table 4: Free-vocabulary AUROC by number of peer families on development set E.</p>
    <div class="table-wrap">
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>k</th><th>AUROC (overall)</th><th>AUROC (long, T3)</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>1</td><td>0.685</td><td>0.581</td></tr>
          <tr><td>3</td><td>0.757</td><td>0.651</td></tr>
          <tr><td>5</td><td>0.776</td><td>0.698</td></tr>
          <tr><td>7</td><td>0.784</td><td>0.726</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="confirmation">
    <h3>Confirmation status</h3>
    <p>Independent confirmation on held-out data remains incomplete. A fresh held-out dataset (E2-A, 550 new sentences) was constructed, but the run-level budget was exhausted before enough items could be labelled. On the one testable stratum (DT, short sentences from ProverQA), consensus achieves 0.916, tying the local Qwen-8B judge (&Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.003 [&minus;0.042, +0.052]). On L25 sentences, <code>c_score_align</code> falls to 0.443 on only 42 items (35 ERROR / 7 CORRECT), but with extreme variance from only 7 CORRECT items across 3 sentences. Every pre-registered criterion on the target strata returned NOT_TESTABLE or unfavourable.</p>
  </section>

  <section id="rename">
    <h3>The rename tradeoff</h3>
    <p>When correct formulas are copied with meaning-preserving predicate renames, the consensus score should not change. In practice it does:</p>
    <p class="table-cap">Table 5: False-alarm (FA) rates on meaning-preserving renames of CORRECT candidates. NONCE = random nonsense names; SYN = WordNet synonyms. Flip = FA induced by the rename alone.</p>
    <div class="table-wrap">
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>NONCE FA</th><th>NONCE flip</th><th>SYN FA</th><th>SYN flip</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>c_align</code></td><td>0.765</td><td>0.605</td><td>0.565</td><td>0.313</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>c_nf</code> (name-free)</td><td>0.132</td><td>0.000</td><td>0.201</td><td>0.000</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>p_peer_text</code></td><td>1.000</td><td>0.821</td><td>0.216</td><td>0.080</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Judge (disg.)</td><td>0.229</td><td>0.134</td><td>0.085</td><td>0.058</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
    <p>The name-free variant <code>c_nf</code> eliminates rename sensitivity (flip&nbsp;=&nbsp;0) but at the cost of blindness to meaning-rename errors (within-base AUROC 0.499, chance level) and lower overall discrimination (strat AUROC 0.686 vs. 0.741). This tradeoff explains the gap between shared-signature and free-vocabulary performance.</p>
  </section>

  <section id="dead-ends">
    <h3>Dead ends</h3>
    <p>Several alternatives were investigated and abandoned: a fused structural-feature filter (false-alarm gate failure); name-free consensus <code>c_nf</code> (rename-invariant but blind to meaning-rename errors); a decomposed solver-based semantic reader (balanced accuracy 0.476); LLM adjudication of disputed items (balanced accuracy 0.662 on expert-labelled items); and candidate-signature consensus, which cues peers with the candidate's own predicate symbols (error endorsement rose to 0.459 because peers were anchored into reproducing errors).</p>
  </section>
</section>

<section id="limitations">
  <h2>Limitations</h2>
  <ol class="lim-list">
    <li><strong>Shared-signature scope.</strong> The 0.954 AUROC result uses templated sentences with a supplied predicate vocabulary, limiting its scope to controlled evaluation settings.</li>
    <li><strong>Development data overlap.</strong> The R_COMP-SIG dataset later served as development data for aligner tuning. The pre-registration ensures the SIG result is uncontaminated, but the development-set numbers from E are not independent.</li>
    <li><strong>Rename vulnerability.</strong> Under free vocabulary, a 76.5% false-alarm rate on nonce renames systematically penalises any translation using non-standard predicate names.</li>
    <li><strong>Length degradation.</strong> Consensus discrimination degrades with sentence length under free vocabulary (NET +0.356), driven by correct-translation divergence. The metric is weakest on the longest, most complex sentences.</li>
    <li><strong>Provisional labels.</strong> R_COMP FREE results use provisional (non-confirmatory) labels; the two-auditor subset (&Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.105) has a CI that barely excludes zero.</li>
    <li><strong>Label dependence.</strong> Development results depend on a three-person panel whose agreement is imperfect. The metric's advantage could partly reflect alignment with panel biases.</li>
    <li><strong>Cost.</strong> The consensus metric requires generating k peer translations per sentence, costing $0.91 per 10,000 candidates (amortised) at k&nbsp;=&nbsp;9; a single cheap judge call costs $0.51 per 10,000.</li>
    <li><strong>Domain.</strong> All results are on English-to-FOL from MALLS, ProverQA, and R_COMP sources. Generalisation to other logic formalisms, languages, or sentence distributions is untested.</li>
  </ol>
</section>

Preliminary Study</div>\n  <div class=\"hero-tldr\">\n    <strong>TL;DR</strong> &mdash; If independent LLM families translate the same sentence into first-order logic and an SMT solver checks pairwise equivalence, the fraction of peers that disagree with a candidate predicts whether it is faithful to the text. Under shared predicate vocabulary this reaches 0.954 AUROC; under free vocabulary it achieves 0.741 stratified AUROC, outperforming LLM judges by +0.099 on development data without any gold references.\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"hero-links\">\n    <a href=\"paper.pdf\" target=\"_blank\">Paper PDF</a>\n    <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic\" target=\"_blank\">Code repository</a>\n  </div>\n</header>\n\n<section id=\"contributions\">\n  <h2>Contributions</h2>\n  <div class=\"contrib-grid\">\n    <div class=\"contrib-card\">\n      <h3>Shared-signature ceiling</h3>\n      <p>Pre-registered evaluation on 221 long-exception sentences: consensus AUROC 0.954 versus 0.587 for a disguised judge (&Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.367), flat across word-length terciles, with zero error endorsement.</p>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"contrib-card\">\n      <h3>Free-vocabulary signal</h3>\n      <p>On development set&nbsp;E (2,686 items), consensus outperforms judges by &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.099 on stratified AUROC. Aligner-free consensus (c_exact) reaches 0.689 without any predicate mapping.</p>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"contrib-card\">\n      <h3>Out-of-sample transfer</h3>\n      <p>On untouched R_COMP&nbsp;FREE sentences under provisional labels: &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.171 versus the original-view judge; consensus reaches 0.94 of the frontier judge's AUROC.</p>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"contrib-card\">\n      <h3>Rename tradeoff</h3>\n      <p>A 76.5% false-alarm rate under nonce predicate renames that no variant could eliminate without sacrificing error recall, identifying a fundamental limit of free-vocabulary consensus.</p>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n</section>\n\n<section id=\"method\">\n  <h2>Method</h2>\n\n  <h3>Consensus scoring</h3>\n  <p>Given a sentence and a candidate FOL translation, collect peer translations from <em>k</em> independent LLM families. Each peer uses the same few-shot prompt but a different base model (Gemini, Claude, GPT, Llama, Qwen, Phi, Mistral). The consensus score is:</p>\n  <p style=\"text-align:center; font-family: var(--serif); font-size: 1.05rem; margin-block: 0.75rem;\">\n    c_score(c, s) = 1 &minus; (1/k) &Sigma; <b>1</b>[equiv(c, p<sub>i</sub>)]\n  </p>\n  <p>Under <strong>shared signature</strong>, all translators use a supplied predicate vocabulary and equiv is a direct Z3 check. Under <strong>free vocabulary</strong>, each translator chooses its own predicate names and equiv requires a predicate-name aligner before the Z3 check.</p>\n\n  <h3>Predicate alignment</h3>\n  <p>Independent translators choose different names for the same concept (e.g., <code>Runs(x)</code> vs. <code>IsRunner(x)</code>). The aligner combines three cost components: <strong>structural cost</strong> (polarity profile, argument-count match, nesting depth), <strong>text-anchor cost</strong> (overlap between predicate-name words and source-sentence tokens via Porter stemming and WordNet), and <strong>semantic signature</strong> (truth-value profiles over random finite interpretations). The <em>k</em> cheapest bijections are evaluated, and the pair is declared equivalent if any bijection yields Z3-verified equivalence.</p>\n\n  <h3>Score variants</h3>\n  <p><code>c_exact</code>: no alignment, exact-match equivalence only. Immune to rename false alarms but blind to vocabulary-differing equivalences. <code>c_nf</code> (name-free): alignment by structural and semantic signatures only, ignoring text anchoring. <code>p_peer_text</code>: logistic fusion of consensus features with text-side features (bag-of-words coverage, role accounting, Z3 structural match).</p>\n\n  <h3>Evaluation framework</h3>\n  <p><strong>Shared-signature labels</strong> come from Z3 equivalence to trusted-by-construction references, with no human or LLM judgement in the labelling loop. <strong>Free-vocabulary labels</strong> on development set&nbsp;E come from a three-person expert panel (adjudicated as ERROR or CORRECT). The primary metric is <strong>stratified AUROC</strong>: items are paired only within the same source stratum, eliminating confounds from stratum-level base rates. Confidence intervals use sentence-cluster percentile bootstrap (B&nbsp;=&nbsp;2,000).</p>\n</section>\n\n<section id=\"results\">\n  <h2>Results</h2>\n\n  <div class=\"big-nums\">\n    <div class=\"big-num\">\n      <div class=\"val\">0.954</div>\n      <div class=\"label\">Consensus AUROC<br>(shared signature)</div>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"big-num\">\n      <div class=\"val\">0.741</div>\n      <div class=\"label\">Consensus AUROC<br>(free vocabulary, dev)</div>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"big-num\">\n      <div class=\"val\">+0.099</div>\n      <div class=\"label\">&Delta; over judge<br>(free vocabulary, dev)</div>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n\n  <section id=\"sig-results\">\n    <h3>Shared-signature results (R_COMP-SIG)</h3>\n    <p class=\"table-cap\">Table 1: Within-template AUROC on R_COMP-SIG (221 sentences, pure Z3 labels). CIs are 95% sentence-cluster bootstrap.</p>\n    <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>n</th><th>AUROC [95% CI]</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td><code>c_score_sig</code></td><td>2024</td><td>0.952 [0.937, 0.965]</td></tr>\n          <tr><td><code>c_score_align</code></td><td>2024</td><td>0.952 [0.937, 0.965]</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Judge (frontier, orig.)</td><td>60</td><td>0.932 [0.782, 1.000]</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Judge (flash-lite, orig.)</td><td>1932</td><td>0.673 [0.637, 0.708]</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Judge (flash-lite, disg.)</td><td>1904</td><td>0.587 [0.551, 0.622]</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Judge (local, disg.)</td><td>2024</td><td>0.498 [0.459, 0.534]</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n    <p>On 1,904 rows where both scores exist, consensus achieves &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.367 [+0.328, +0.404] over the disguised flash-lite judge. Error endorsement is zero: every error item receives a consensus score of 1.0 (maximum divergence).</p>\n\n    <p><strong>Flat with sentence length.</strong> Unlike the free-vocabulary setting, consensus under shared signature is flat across word-length terciles:</p>\n    <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>Tercile</th><th>n</th><th>ERR/COR</th><th>c_sig</th><th>Judge (disg.)</th><th>&Delta; [CI]</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>W1 (shortest)</td><td>574</td><td>125/449</td><td>0.959</td><td>0.578</td><td>+0.382 [+0.278, +0.472]</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>W2</td><td>743</td><td>149/594</td><td>0.947</td><td>0.624</td><td>+0.331 [+0.253, +0.421]</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>W3 (longest)</td><td>707</td><td>155/552</td><td>0.953</td><td>0.567</td><td>+0.388 [+0.301, +0.471]</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n    <p>On a descriptive 60-row stratified subsample scored by the frontier judge (Gemini 3.1 Pro, original view), consensus achieves pooled AUROC 0.956 [0.889, 1.000] versus 0.932 [0.855, 0.990] for the frontier judge.</p>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"dev-results\">\n    <h3>Free-vocabulary development results (set E)</h3>\n    <p class=\"table-cap\">Table 2: Stratified AUROC on development set E (R_AB population, free vocabulary, n&nbsp;=&nbsp;2,686). Higher is better.</p>\n    <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>Strat AUROC [95% CI]</th><th>$/item</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td><code>c_score_align</code></td><td>0.741 [0.705, 0.775]</td><td>9.1e-5</td></tr>\n          <tr><td><code>p_peer_text</code> (fused)</td><td>0.753 [0.720, 0.784]</td><td>9.1e-5</td></tr>\n          <tr><td><code>c_exact</code> (no alignment)</td><td>0.689 [0.652, 0.726]</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>\n          <tr><td><code>c_nf</code> (name-free)</td><td>0.686 [0.647, 0.720]</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>\n          <tr><td colspan=\"3\" style=\"border:none; padding:0.25rem\"></td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Flash-lite judge (disg.)</td><td>0.642 [0.607, 0.676]</td><td>5.1e-5</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Flash-lite judge (orig.)</td><td>0.623 [0.593, 0.651]</td><td>5.1e-5</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Nano judge (disg.)</td><td>0.644 [0.609, 0.680]</td><td>2.0e-5</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Local judge Qwen-8B (disg.)</td><td>0.674 [0.646, 0.703]</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>\n          <tr><td colspan=\"3\" style=\"border:none; padding:0.25rem\"></td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Round-trip NLI (min)</td><td>0.606 [0.569, 0.645]</td><td>2.8e-5</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Self-consistency (5-sample)</td><td>0.598 [0.559, 0.637]</td><td>6.7e-5</td></tr>\n          <tr><td colspan=\"3\" style=\"border:none; padding:0.25rem\"></td></tr>\n          <tr><td>28-feature stack</td><td>0.735 [0.699, 0.766]</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>28-feature stack + <code>c_score_align</code></td><td>0.774 [0.743, 0.802]</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n    <p>Cross-family consensus outperforms the disguised flash-lite judge by &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.099 [+0.049, +0.146] on the full R_AB population and by &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.116 [+0.070, +0.163] on the long-sentence pool (L25+L20+EXC). Adding <code>c_score_align</code> to the 28-feature baseline stack increases stratified AUROC by +0.039 [+0.021, +0.057]; a permutation null test gives p<sub>95</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.009.</p>\n    <p>The drop from 0.952 (shared signature) to 0.741 (free vocabulary) reflects the cost of predicate-name alignment. Aligner-free consensus (<code>c_exact</code>) at 0.689 indicates that roughly half of the free-vocabulary signal comes from structural agreement alone.</p>\n    <p>On L25 sentences alone, the advantage narrows to &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.069 [&minus;0.020, +0.148], not significant at the 95% level. The frontier judge comparison on a 284-row subsample shows <code>c_score_align</code> at 95.7% of the frontier judge's AUROC (ratio 0.957 [0.887, 1.034]).</p>\n    <p>System-level ranking: Kendall &tau;<sub>b</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.692 [+0.513, +0.795] between system mean score and R_AB error rate across 13 system&times;variant configurations.</p>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"oos-results\">\n    <h3>Free-vocabulary out-of-sample (R_COMP FREE)</h3>\n    <p class=\"table-cap\">Table 3: R_COMP FREE provisional AUROCs (within-template, untouched rows). Labels are non-confirmatory.</p>\n    <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>View</th><th>n (ERR/MAPPED)</th><th>c_align</th><th>Judge</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>Disguised</td><td>1706 (602/1104)</td><td>0.801 [0.770, 0.834]</td><td>0.584 [0.550, 0.618]</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Original</td><td>1709 (605/1104)</td><td>0.804 [0.774, 0.836]</td><td>0.633 [0.601, 0.666]</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n    <p>The disguised-judge delta is +0.217 [+0.175, +0.260]; the original-view delta is +0.171 [+0.135, +0.206]. On a 146-row subset with independent two-auditor labels, &Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.105 [+0.011, +0.215]. On a 150-row frontier-judge subsample, consensus reaches 0.94 of the frontier judge's AUROC (ratio 0.940 [0.825, 1.056]).</p>\n    <p>These provisional numbers cannot count as confirmation because the MAPPED labels conflate vocabulary-alignment failures with genuine correctness.</p>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"mechanism\">\n    <h3>Mechanism</h3>\n    <p>The consensus signal decomposes into endorsement <em>e</em> (fraction of ERROR items endorsed by the peer majority) and divergence <em>d</em> (fraction of CORRECT items flagged). On R_COMP-SIG, <em>e</em>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.0 and <em>d</em>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.260: no error escapes detection.</p>\n    <p>Under free vocabulary on development set E, the net degradation from short to long sentences is &Delta;(e+d)&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.356 [+0.198, +0.493], driven almost entirely by divergence (&Delta;d&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.608, &Delta;e&nbsp;=&nbsp;&minus;0.252). Correct translations of long sentences increasingly disagree with their peers due to different structural choices for complex quantifier scopes and exception clauses.</p>\n\n    <p><strong>Family sufficiency.</strong> Three peer families suffice for 97% of full-pool AUROC (k<sub>95</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;3), but the long-sentence tercile requires k<sub>95</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;5.</p>\n    <p class=\"table-cap\">Table 4: Free-vocabulary AUROC by number of peer families on development set E.</p>\n    <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>k</th><th>AUROC (overall)</th><th>AUROC (long, T3)</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>1</td><td>0.685</td><td>0.581</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>3</td><td>0.757</td><td>0.651</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>5</td><td>0.776</td><td>0.698</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>7</td><td>0.784</td><td>0.726</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"confirmation\">\n    <h3>Confirmation status</h3>\n    <p>Independent confirmation on held-out data remains incomplete. A fresh held-out dataset (E2-A, 550 new sentences) was constructed, but the run-level budget was exhausted before enough items could be labelled. On the one testable stratum (DT, short sentences from ProverQA), consensus achieves 0.916, tying the local Qwen-8B judge (&Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.003 [&minus;0.042, +0.052]). On L25 sentences, <code>c_score_align</code> falls to 0.443 on only 42 items (35 ERROR / 7 CORRECT), but with extreme variance from only 7 CORRECT items across 3 sentences. Every pre-registered criterion on the target strata returned NOT_TESTABLE or unfavourable.</p>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"rename\">\n    <h3>The rename tradeoff</h3>\n    <p>When correct formulas are copied with meaning-preserving predicate renames, the consensus score should not change. In practice it does:</p>\n    <p class=\"table-cap\">Table 5: False-alarm (FA) rates on meaning-preserving renames of CORRECT candidates. NONCE = random nonsense names; SYN = WordNet synonyms. Flip = FA induced by the rename alone.</p>\n    <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>NONCE FA</th><th>NONCE flip</th><th>SYN FA</th><th>SYN flip</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td><code>c_align</code></td><td>0.765</td><td>0.605</td><td>0.565</td><td>0.313</td></tr>\n          <tr><td><code>c_nf</code> (name-free)</td><td>0.132</td><td>0.000</td><td>0.201</td><td>0.000</td></tr>\n          <tr><td><code>p_peer_text</code></td><td>1.000</td><td>0.821</td><td>0.216</td><td>0.080</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Judge (disg.)</td><td>0.229</td><td>0.134</td><td>0.085</td><td>0.058</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n    <p>The name-free variant <code>c_nf</code> eliminates rename sensitivity (flip&nbsp;=&nbsp;0) but at the cost of blindness to meaning-rename errors (within-base AUROC 0.499, chance level) and lower overall discrimination (strat AUROC 0.686 vs. 0.741). This tradeoff explains the gap between shared-signature and free-vocabulary performance.</p>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"dead-ends\">\n    <h3>Dead ends</h3>\n    <p>Several alternatives were investigated and abandoned: a fused structural-feature filter (false-alarm gate failure); name-free consensus <code>c_nf</code> (rename-invariant but blind to meaning-rename errors); a decomposed solver-based semantic reader (balanced accuracy 0.476); LLM adjudication of disputed items (balanced accuracy 0.662 on expert-labelled items); and candidate-signature consensus, which cues peers with the candidate's own predicate symbols (error endorsement rose to 0.459 because peers were anchored into reproducing errors).</p>\n  </section>\n</section>\n\n<section id=\"figures\">\n  <h2>Figures</h2>\n  <div class=\"fig-gallery\">\n    <figure class=\"fig-card\" tabindex=\"0\" role=\"button\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 1\">\n      <img src=\"figures/fig_dev_auroc_v0.png\"\n           alt=\"Horizontal bar chart comparing stratified AUROC across 12 metrics on the free-vocabulary development set. Consensus-based metrics (blue bars) cluster around 0.69 to 0.77; LLM judges (orange) around 0.62 to 0.67; other baselines (grey) near 0.60.\">\n      <figcaption class=\"fig-caption\">Fig. 1: Stratified AUROC on the free-vocabulary development set for main metrics and baselines.</figcaption>\n      <p class=\"fig-hint\">Click to enlarge</p>\n    </figure>\n    <figure class=\"fig-card\" tabindex=\"0\" role=\"button\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 2\">\n      <img src=\"figures/fig_complexity_v0.png\"\n           alt=\"Bar chart decomposing consensus errors by sentence-length tercile. Endorsement rate e decreases from 0.29 to 0.04 while divergence rate d increases from 0.31 to 0.91. Dashed net line (e+d) rises by +0.356 from shortest to longest tercile.\">\n      <figcaption class=\"fig-caption\">Fig. 2: Decomposition of consensus error rates by sentence-length tercile. Net degradation &Delta;(e+d) = +0.356.</figcaption>\n      <p class=\"fig-hint\">Click to enlarge</p>\n    </figure>\n    <figure class=\"fig-card\" tabindex=\"0\" role=\"button\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 3\">\n      <img src=\"figures/fig_k_curve_v0.png\"\n           alt=\"Line chart of AUROC vs number of peer families k. Overall curve (solid) rises steeply to k=3 then flattens; long-sentence tercile (dashed) rises more slowly, requiring k=5 to reach 95% of full-pool signal.\">\n      <figcaption class=\"fig-caption\">Fig. 3: AUROC as a function of the number of peer families k. Three families capture 97% of the full-pool signal; long sentences require five.</figcaption>\n      <p class=\"fig-hint\">Click to enlarge</p>\n    </figure>\n  </div>\n</section>\n\n<section id=\"limitations\">\n  <h2>Limitations</h2>\n  <ol class=\"lim-list\">\n    <li><strong>Shared-signature scope.</strong> The 0.954 AUROC result uses templated sentences with a supplied predicate vocabulary, limiting its scope to controlled evaluation settings.</li>\n    <li><strong>Development data overlap.</strong> The R_COMP-SIG dataset later served as development data for aligner tuning. The pre-registration ensures the SIG result is uncontaminated, but the development-set numbers from E are not independent.</li>\n    <li><strong>Rename vulnerability.</strong> Under free vocabulary, a 76.5% false-alarm rate on nonce renames systematically penalises any translation using non-standard predicate names.</li>\n    <li><strong>Length degradation.</strong> Consensus discrimination degrades with sentence length under free vocabulary (NET +0.356), driven by correct-translation divergence. The metric is weakest on the longest, most complex sentences.</li>\n    <li><strong>Provisional labels.</strong> R_COMP FREE results use provisional (non-confirmatory) labels; the two-auditor subset (&Delta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.105) has a CI that barely excludes zero.</li>\n    <li><strong>Label dependence.</strong> Development results depend on a three-person panel whose agreement is imperfect. The metric's advantage could partly reflect alignment with panel biases.</li>\n    <li><strong>Cost.</strong> The consensus metric requires generating k peer translations per sentence, costing $0.91 per 10,000 candidates (amortised) at k&nbsp;=&nbsp;9; a single cheap judge call costs $0.51 per 10,000.</li>\n    <li><strong>Domain.</strong> All results are on English-to-FOL from MALLS, ProverQA, and R_COMP sources. Gold-Free Faithfulness Metric for Natural-Language-to-First-Order-Logic
Translation*.

## What this is

A single self-contained HTML page that presents the paper's contributions,
method, results, and figures faster than reading the PDF. Designed to be
served directly from GitHub Pages with no build step.

## Repository layout

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `index.html` | Self-contained project page (inline CSS/JS, no external deps except Google Fonts) |
| `paper.tex` | LaTeX source of the paper |
| `paper.pdf` | Compiled PDF |
| `references.bib` | BibTeX bibliography |
| `references.json` | Structured bibliography in JSON |
| `figures/*.png` | Rendered figures used by the project page |
| `figures/*.pdf` | Vector figure originals |
| `figures/*_spec.json` | Figure generation specifications |

## Viewing the page

Open `index.html` in any modern browser, or visit the GitHub Pages deployment.
No build step, server, or external resources beyond Google Fonts are required.

## License

See the paper for terms.
